entry.title: Why, after 20 years as a JavaScript developer, I switched to semicolons
entry.summary:
This is a first of a series I thought I'd start writing (and hopefully continue writing) about my experiences over 36 years as a programmer, and 20+ years as a professional web developer. (Am I old now? I think I'm old.) First, what are we talking about? If you're new to JavaScript, you may know that JavaScript is rather forgiving of statement terminations. JavaScript isn't alone in this. Go, Swift, Kotlin, Ruby, Python, Lua... they all make semicolons optional at the end of statements. In JavaScript, the spec calls this Automatic Semicolon Insertion or ASI. The simplified explanation is that if JS sees what would be a syntax error, and it thinks a semicolon might fix it, it inserts one automatically. Here's an example: let one = 1 let two = 2
